written.description: Judges an MCP server's tool definitions three ways, by YARA rule, by hosted inspection API and by asking a model, so a poisoned tool description has to clear more than one kind of reader.

alive.last_commit_message:
Fix : TS dynamic tool registration extraction for wrappers  (#233)

* Fix TS dynamic tool registration extraction for wrappers, bind, and loops.

Resolve safeTool-style wrappers, bound class methods, forEach table expansion, and cross-file endpoint loops so static scans report literal tool names instead of parameter or member-expression stubs.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* Address CodeRabbit review on scoped table suppression and wrappers.

Scope loop-based registration deduplication to table-producing for/forEach sites, read TS parameter names via pattern field, and preserve prompt/resource capability kinds for wrapper delegations.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* Strengthen dynamic registration test and preserve member-expression names.

Track name_ref for tool names like config.name in registration output and assert the independent dynamic registration is retained separately from table-expanded tools.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* Wire cross-file call graphs into JSBehavioralCodeAnalyzer directory scans.

Build TreeSitterCallGraphAnalyzer per language when scanning JS/TS
directories so NativeAnalyzer can resolve imported endpoint tables
(pattern 09b: tool.alias → list-mail / get-calendar) in npm and registry paths.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* fix(static): address PR review on TS table loops and receiver trust

Preserve inline handler evidence for table-driven registrations, resolve
bind() handlers against receiver classes, require MCP calls inside loops
before expanding tables, tighten trusted receiver matching, ignore
shadowed wrapper parameters, and cap JS call-graph build budgets.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* fix(js): release call-graph source cache after per-file analysis

Only populate _source_cache during the budgeted call-graph build and pop
entries in _analyze_file so large directory scans do not retain every
source in memory for the full scan.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* fix: resolve local shadows and bound call-graph resources

Addresses two review comments on #233.

Wrapper shadow resolution (native_analyzer.py)

Wrapper registration detection recognised only parameter shadowing, so a
local rebinding of the wrapper name was taken for the module-level MCP
wrapper. `const safeTool = other` inside a helper emitted a ghost
capability carrying that helper's evidence, including an eval the real
wrapper never reaches.

`_ts_is_parameter_shadow` is replaced by `_ts_is_local_shadow`, which
checks each enclosing function scope for a parameter or a local
declaration rebinding the name. Local bindings cover const/let/var,
destructuring (including renamed `{ impl: safeTool }`, where only the
value side binds), and nested function declarations. Enclosing scopes are
now walked to the root rather than stopping at the innermost function, so
an outer-scope shadow is caught too.

Genuine module-level registrations are unaffected: a wrapper call with no
local rebinding still registers.

Resource controls (js_code_analyzer.py, treesitter_call_graph.py)

File and byte budgets bounded how much source was read but not what it
expanded into, nor the cost of finding it.

Discovery is bounded on two axes: matched files, and directory entries
examined, so a few sources buried under a very large tree cannot make the
walk itself expensive. Filter rules still mirror `count_source_files`, so
the reported total stays truthful and the partial flag records that not
all of it was analysed.

The call-graph builder gains AST-node, function, edge and wall-clock
budgets. Exceeding any sets `budget_exceeded`, which the JS analyzer folds
into the existing `call_graph_partial` signal, so a truncated graph is
never reported as complete. A failed build is now partial rather than
silently empty.

Parse trees and source bytes are released once the directory scan
finishes. They are needed for the whole scan, not just the build, because
cross-file handler and endpoint-table resolution reads them per file.

TSCallGraph also gains callee/caller adjacency indexes. Reachability
previously rescanned the full edge list per lookup, which is O(V*E) on
densely connected graphs and the CPU blow-up that edge caps alone would
not prevent.

Adds 15 tests covering each shadow form, each budget, source release
keeping the built graph usable, and index/edge-list agreement.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
